lessons.title: ശ (śa) — the letter that opens ശരി
lessons.gloss: śa — the letter that opens ശരി

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ശ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ഠ and ഫ once each, and name them.
Now say ശരി (śari), "okay". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ശ — śa, the sound sh.
It opens ശരി (śari), "okay", one of the first words in this book.
Put your pen on ശ (śa) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start this letter or which way to travel. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.

segments.instruction: at ശരി and point at ശ (śa) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **ശരി** and point at ശ inside it]

segments.instruction: ശ (śa) three times, saying ś as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: ശ three times, saying *ś* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ഫ, then ശ, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — ശ? (śa, ś.) Which word did it come from? (ശരി, śari, "okay".)

segments.text: Before the new one: write ഫ and ശ (śa) once each, and name them.
Now say നിങ്ങൾ (niṅṅaḷ), "you (respectful)". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ങ — ṅa, the nasal made where k is made.
It is inside നിങ്ങൾ (niṅṅaḷ), the respectful "you", where it is written twice, one on top of the other, for the long ṅṅ.
Put your pen on ങ (ṅa) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start this letter or which way to travel. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ശ (śa) and ങ (ṅa) once each, and name them.
Now say നാളെ (nāḷe), "tomorrow". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ള — ḷa, an l made with the tongue curled back.
It is inside നാളെ (nāḷe), "tomorrow", from നാളെ കാണാം, "see you tomorrow". The dot under the romanization (ḷ) is what marks the curled tongue.
Put your pen on ള (ḷa) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start this letter or which way to travel. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.

ഖ — kha, a k with a puff of breath.
It is inside സുഖമാണോ? (sukhamāṇō?), "how are you?", built on സുഖം (sukham), "well-being".
Put your pen on ഖ (kha) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.
